title: Clergy Act

claims.claim: Ordained ministers can apply to opt out of Social Security taxes on ministerial earnings via the section 1402(e)(1) exemption
claims.sourceSpan: any exemption which has been received under section 1402(e)(1) of such Code by a duly ordained, commissioned, or licensed minister of a church

claims.claim: Christian Science practitioners are among those covered by the exemption
claims.sourceSpan: or a Christian Science practitioner

claims.claim: The exemption also covers Medicare taxes
claims.sourceSpan: may revoke their exemption from Social Security coverage
claims.note: Source frames the exemption solely as Social Security coverage (title II); the word 'Medicare' and any title XVIII / Hospital-Insurance reference are absent from the source.

claims.claim: That exemption is currently irrevocable
claims.sourceSpan: Notwithstanding section 1402(e)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986
claims.note: Irrevocability is a reasonable inference from the 'notwithstanding' clause plus the no-refiling bar, but the source never states that 1402(e)(4) makes the exemption irrevocable.

claims.claim: Creates a one-time window for prior opt-outs to reverse that decision and re-enter Social Security
claims.sourceSpan: may be revoked by filing an application therefor

claims.claim: Coverage begins for taxable years starting after December 31, 2027
claims.sourceSpan: in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027

claims.claim: Once revoked, they cannot opt out again
claims.sourceSpan: may not thereafter again file an application for an exemption under such section 1402(e)(1)

claims.claim: Creates a one-time window for clergy who opted out of Social Security to reverse that decision
claims.sourceSpan: may be revoked by filing an application therefor

claims.claim: Revoking lets them begin accruing retirement benefits
claims.sourceSpan: monthly insurance benefits payable under title II of the Social Security Act
claims.note: Title II monthly insurance benefits reasonably rendered in lay terms as retirement benefits.

claims.claim: One-Time Re-entry Window
claims.sourceSpan: may not thereafter again file an application for an exemption under such section 1402(e)(1)

claims.claim: Clergy may revoke by filing through the deadline for their second taxable year beginning after December 31, 2027
claims.sourceSpan: filed no later than the due date of the Federal income tax return (including any extension thereof) for the applicant’s second taxable year beginning after December 31, 2027

claims.claim: Coverage begins for taxable years starting after December 31, 2027
claims.sourceSpan: in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027

claims.claim: Cannot opt out again after revoking
claims.sourceSpan: may not thereafter again file an application for an exemption under such section 1402(e)(1)

claims.claim: IRS Outreach Required
claims.sourceSpan: shall develop and submit to the Committee on Ways and Means

claims.claim: Commissioner of Internal Revenue must submit a plan to inform eligible clergy of their eligibility within 90 days of enactment
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Commissioner of Internal Revenue

claims.claim: Names the Act the Clergy Act
claims.sourceSpan: This Act may be cited as the Clergy Act

claims.claim: Short-title section; citation name only, no substantive effect
claims.sourceSpan: Short title

claims.claim: Revocation operates notwithstanding section 1402(e)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code
claims.sourceSpan: Notwithstanding section 1402(e)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986

claims.claim: Section 1402(e)(4) makes the Social Security exemption irrevocable
claims.sourceSpan: Notwithstanding section 1402(e)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986
claims.note: Parenthetical gloss on the content of an unfetched statute; source shows only the 'notwithstanding' override, not that 1402(e)(4) is the irrevocability provision.

claims.claim: Applies to clergy whose exemption is in effect for the taxable year of enactment
claims.sourceSpan: which is effective for the taxable year in which this Act is enacted

claims.claim: They may revoke by filing an application with the IRS
claims.sourceSpan: may be revoked by filing an application therefor (in such form and manner, and with such official, as may be prescribed by the Commissioner of Internal Revenue)

claims.claim: Application must be filed no later than the due date for the second taxable year beginning after December 31, 2027
claims.sourceSpan: filed no later than the due date of the Federal income tax return (including any extension thereof) for the applicant’s second taxable year beginning after December 31, 2027

claims.claim: Revocation takes effect for the first or second taxable year beginning after December 31, 2027, as specified by the applicant
claims.sourceSpan: either with respect to the applicant’s first taxable year beginning after December 31, 2027, or with respect to the applicant’s second taxable year beginning after such date

claims.claim: Covers both chapter 2 of the IRC and title II of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 401 et seq.)
claims.sourceSpan: chapter 2 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 and title II of the Social Security Act

claims.claim: Chapter 2 is the self-employment tax
claims.sourceSpan: net earnings from self-employment for purposes of chapter 2 of such Code

claims.claim: A retroactive election for a past year requires payment in full of all self-employment taxes that would have been owed for that year
claims.sourceSpan: it shall include or be accompanied by payment in full of an amount equal to the total of the taxes that would have been imposed by section 1401 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986

claims.claim: After revoking, the applicant may not again file for an exemption under section 1402(e)(1)
claims.sourceSpan: may not thereafter again file an application for an exemption under such section 1402(e)(1)

claims.claim: Commissioner of Internal Revenue, in consultation with the Commissioner of Social Security, must develop and submit a plan to inform eligible clergy of revocation eligibility
claims.sourceSpan: the Commissioner of Internal Revenue, in consultation with the Commissioner of Social Security, shall develop and submit

claims.claim: Plan must inform clergy of their eligibility to revoke a prior exemption election, within 90 days of enactment
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Plan must be submitted to the House Ways and Means Committee and the Senate Finance Committee
claims.sourceSpan: the Committee on Ways and Means of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Finance of the Senate

claims.claim: No minimum outreach activities, funding level, or success metrics are specified in the bill
claims.sourceSpan: a plan to inform duly ordained, commissioned, or licensed ministers of a church
claims.note: Section 3 prescribes only 'a plan'; the source states no minimum activities, funding, or metrics -- accurate negative.

claims.claim: One-time window for clergy and Christian Science practitioners to revoke their exemption under section 1402(e)(1)
claims.sourceSpan: any exemption which has been received under section 1402(e)(1) of such Code by a duly ordained, commissioned, or licensed minister of a church, a member of a religious order, or a Christian Science practitioner

claims.claim: The revoked exemption is described as irrevocable
claims.sourceSpan: Notwithstanding section 1402(e)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986
claims.note: Same inference as summary; irrevocability not explicitly stated in source.

claims.claim: Effective for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027
claims.sourceSpan: in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027

claims.claim: Requirement for the Commissioner of Internal Revenue to submit an outreach plan within 90 days of enactment
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Commissioner of Internal Revenue

claims.claim: Sponsors include Fong (CA), Thompson (CA), and Kelly (PA)
claims.sourceSpan: Mr. Fong (for himself, Mr. Thompson of California
claims.note: States for Thompson (CA) and Kelly (PA) appear in source; party labels are Congress.gov metadata.

claims.claim: The bill has 21 cosponsors
claims.sourceSpan: Mr. Fong (for himself, Mr. Thompson of California
claims.note: Cosponsor count is Congress.gov metadata (cache cosponsors:21), not in the bill text, which names only the three original sponsors; permitted structural metadata.

claims.claim: Bipartisan backing
claims.sourceSpan: Mr. Thompson of California
claims.note: Cross-party sponsorship (Fong/Kelly R, Thompson D); structural, party labels are metadata.

claims.claim: Providing a window to undo a permanent decision is unlikely to draw opposition; narrow scope and sympathetic population make Senate passage plausible
claims.sourceSpan: may revoke their exemption from Social Security coverage
claims.note: Analytical likelihood assessment, not a source claim; permitted as likelihood reasoning with no breadth-of-support overreach.

claims.claim: Filing a revocation after the due date and electing that year triggers immediate payment of all self-employment taxes that would have been owed for the entire year
claims.sourceSpan: If the application is filed after the due date of the applicant’s Federal income tax return for a taxable year and is effective with respect to that taxable year, it shall include or be accompanied by payment in full

claims.claim: Revocation is effective for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027
claims.sourceSpan: in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027

claims.claim: The bill does not address Social Security credits for prior exempt years; those years generate no credits regardless of revocation
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply with respect to service performed (to the extent specified in such subsection) in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027
claims.note: Forward-only effective date supports that pre-2028 service is not covered; the specific 'no Social Security credits' mechanics are extrinsic to the source.

claims.claim: The 90-day outreach plan specifies no minimum activities, channels, or funding, leaving scope to agency discretion
claims.sourceSpan: a plan to inform duly ordained, commissioned, or licensed ministers of a church
claims.note: Accurate negative; Section 3 prescribes only a plan.

claims.claim: Source covers three categories (ordained/commissioned/licensed minister, member of a religious order, Christian Science practitioner); summary lists only 'Ordained ministers and Christian Science practitioners', omitting 'member of a religious order'
claims.sourceSpan: a member of a religious order
claims.note: Reasonably subsumed under the umbrella term 'clergy' used elsewhere; minor.

claims.claim: Section 2(b) also extends revocation effects to lump-sum death payments under title II, not only monthly insurance benefits; not surfaced in the analysis
claims.sourceSpan: lump-sum death payments payable under such title
claims.note: Detail-level; core benefit re-entry is covered.
